title: HierSVA: A Data Synthesis Pipeline, Dataset, and Benchmark for LLM-Generated SystemVerilog Assertions on Hierarchical RTL
claim: A hierarchical design can be represented two ways: an instance tree that duplicates repeated parts, or a compact dependency graph that merges them.
layout: 2 panels side by side, top-down trees, color-coded repeated nodes
description: Two side-by-side panels show the same small hierarchical design in two representations. Panel (a) is an instance tree. A dark 'top' root node branches to modules A (instance u_a) and B (instance u_b). A has one child, X with W=8, drawn in orange. B has three children: X with W=16 in orange, and Y instances u_y0 and u_y1 in green. Each node is a separate instance. Panel (b) is a module dependency graph with one node per module definition, labeled with depth: top d2, A d1, B d1, X d0 and Y d0. Both A and B point to the single X node. The colors mark the two cases from the caption: orange for a module instantiated with two values of W, green for two copies inside one parent. Thin gray arrows and a vertical divider separate the panels. The eye goes first to the dark root node.
caption: (a) Instance tree with one node per instance. (b) Module dependency graph with one node per module definition and its depth (d). Orange marks a module instantiated with two values of $W$, and green marks two copies in one parent.
abstract: We present HierSVA, an integrated suite that combines a data synthesis pipeline, a dataset, and a benchmark for LLM-generated SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) on hierarchical RTL. HierSVA-SP pairs an RTL preprocessing toolchain with an LLM-in-the-loop formal verification flow to produce reference SVA on hierarchical RTL. Applying it to BaseJump STL yields HierSVA-DS, a dataset of 342 modules with hierarchy metadata, accompanied by a deep subset of 28 module-bug pairs with natural-language specifications and bug variants. HierSVA-B decomposes assertion quality into six metric axes: syntax correctness, assertion proof success rate, vacuity, specification faithfulness, mutation coverage, and formal core coverage. Applying HierSVA-B to twelve recent LLMs reveals three findings. First, averaged across models, the module-level compile rate is 66.6\%, and 82.1\% of generated assertions in evaluable runs prove non-vacuously, but the assertion sets detect only 70.2\% of eligible injected faults and cover 36.2\% of the formal core. Second, on 211 evaluable model--module entries in the deep subset, generated assertions flag buggy RTL with 0.87 recall, but 40\% of predicted-buggy outcomes are false positives on correct RTL, limiting precision to 0.60. Third, agentic mode improves provability, but strength metrics do not improve consistently and oscillate across iterations. We release dataset at https://huggingface.co/datasets/AnonymousHierSVA/HierSVA, and also codes and artifacts at https://github.com/HierSVAAnon/HierSVACodeAndArtifacts.
